477: Renton Thurston is the son of the late military hero Adroc Thurston and co-pilot of the Nirvash typeZERO. He has been in love with Eureka the other pilot of the Nirvash ever since he first saw her.
1511: Will is a young man who lives somewhat close to Gianas. He nurses Renton back to health while he was returning to the Gekko. He is a bit talkative, yet insightful and empathetic, preferring to work with nature rather than dominate it.
1512: Holland Novak is the leader of Gekkostate, captain of the Gekko, and pilot of the LFO Terminus typeR909 (and later the Terminus B303).
1530: Talho Yūki is the head pilot of the Gekko. She is also best friends with Hilda. She and Holland are romantically involved throughout the series, with context suggesting that the relationship goes back at least to Holland's military service.
1709: Eureka is a member of Gekkostate and the pilot of the Nirvash type ZERO, alongside her co-pilot Renton Thurston. A bit of an enigma, Eureka is a young girl who has trouble communicating with and understanding people.
1910: Dominic Sorel is the youngest to be second lieutenant and Dewey's subordinate. He is assigned to Anemone to tend to her needs and monitor her physical and mental condition. It's never explained why Dominic was promoted so fast, especially given his occasional naivete.
1911: Anemone is a soldier of the United Federation and the pilot of the Nirvash typeTheEND. She regularly suffers from painful headaches, nose bleeds, and emotional instability, most of which can be temporarily treated with a drug injected into a receptor in her neck.
2920: Matthieu is the easygoing, afro-haired pilot of the Terminus typeR606. He has a passion for music, and seems to be constantly bored. Matthieu seems to be responsible for gathering information from and maintaining contacts with ref boarders and DJs.
3967: Jurgens is the captain of the military airborne battleship "Izumo". While he may seem like a dog of the military he is actually quite contemplative of his job.
4005: A former lieutenant colonel and Holland's brother, Dewey was imprisoned as punishment for Holland and the SOF's desertion, for which they believed him to be responsible. This is also apparently part of the attempt to shut down the remnants Adrock Thurston's project.
4048: A physician aboard the Gekko. She has known Eureka since her days in the military. She will tell anyone what they need to hear, be it cold hard truth, or kind compassion.
4049: Maurice is an orphan adopted by Eureka. She found him under a pile of corpses during the massacre at Ciudades del Cielo.
4679: Perpetually happy, and devoted to Moondoggy. She freely gives advice, but is a bit ditzy. She has no military background, but has taken her place on the bridge of the Gekko as communications operator.
5132: Norb is a powerful Vodarac priest. He can be considered the main influence towards Holland leaving the SOF after Norb explains to him what Dewey is trying to do and the consequences it entailed for the planet and humanity.
5552: Charles Beams is a freelance LFO pilot and mercenary, with his partner and wife Ray.
5896: Sakuya is Eureka's predecessor, sporting lavender hair. Because she was a girl of mysterious power, the religious authority of Vodarac thought she was some sort of messiah and placed her in the central part of the temple.
6718: Wife of Charles Beams, Retired SOF and electronic warfare specialist.
6775: Hap has been a close friend to Holland since their childhood. He is a source of good advice for Holland and helped convince him to leave the military. He got his nickname from his happy smile and easygoing nature.
6779: Renton's Grandfather is a skilled mechanic but cantankerous with people in general. He does not want Renton to follow the life of Renton's father, Adrock, or his sister, Diane.
6794: A professional photographer who is ethically against violence. Has chosen to join Gekkostate to bring a record of what is happening between the military, the Coralians, and the Gekkostate, using the underground magazine Ray=Out.
7105: Ken-Goh is the man responsible for Holland having the Gekko. He serves as weapons system operator on the bridge, but often shouts tactical directions to the other members on the bridge, particularly the pilot. He is extremely stern, but backs it up by knowing what he's doing.
7106: Hilda doesn't seem to have been in the military prior to joining the Gekkostate, but she's a natural lifter. This combined with her quick thinking has made her the best LFO pilot not part of the original group.
9061: Moondoggie is the second-newest member of the Gekkostate (the newest being Renton).
12368: Living up to his name, Jobs does the random jobs on the Gekko and also manages the majority of the hardware aboard the Gekko. Primarily, he's Gekko's engineer and often is found around the core systems room when the ship is requires extra attention in powered flights or battles.
12570: Woz is sometimes called "Woz the Whiz." He is the ship's hacker and maintains the ship's software. He and Jobs were originally stowaways aboard the Gekko, but they were invited to stay because of their technical skills.
17776: Eureka's adopted daughter. (debut of Eureka Seven) - 6 (end of Eureka Seven)
21342: Nicknamed "Dr. Bear" for his physically huge body, Greg Egan is an iconoclastic scientist who was also part of the Tresor research team that initially studied Eureka and her relationship with the Nirvash.
37431: Diane Thurston is Axel's granddaughter and Renton's older sister. She and Axel were the ones who raised Renton after Adroc's death. She left home some years ago, and for initially unexplained reasons her family has not heard from her since.
49999: Renton's uncle, he owned a Punchanut Plantation and had a habit of lying to others for his own gain.
50035: Neal is a Skyfish fisher and son of also Skyfish fisher named Edmond. He and his father's main occupation involved using the Skyfish to create panels for ships such as the Gekko-Go, but it was not a lucrative business, so Neal lost interest in it and turned to alcohol.
50427: A very interesting character in the sense that he knew the name of Thurston not by the last name of his father, but by his grandfather Axel. They met him while they were repairing the ship in the cave, and as a result, made friends with the crew.
50429: Martha is William B. Baxter's wife.
50497: Another of Tresor's scientists, Sonia Wakabayashi formerly studied Eureka along with Mischa. While apparently a good friend to Eureka, she's rather high-strung, and not as adaptable to the Gekkostate lifestyle as Mischa is.
50499: Morita is the head of the Tresor military research complex. He was one of the scientists who studied the first Archetype after its unearthing and worked on both versions of the Nirvash typeZERO.
50701: One of the three sages in The Council of the Sages.
50989: Maria Schneider is the executive officer of the Izumo and trusted right-hand woman of Jurgens. In the movie version of Eureka Seven she's named only as Maria and is married to Jurgens.
50991: Braya is one of the three sages in The Council of the Sages. In the movie version of Eureka Seven he's the Prime Minister of the Central People's Government and Coda Lovell's ex-husband.
50993: Kuzemi is one of the three sages at The Council of the Sages. In the movie version of Eureka Seven he's the Minister of health of the Central People's Government.
